correctness.rationale: The Hardy monomial basis yields the exact injective partial permutation n -> an/b for b|n. Coprimeness gives unique maximal a,b divisor exponents; for a,b>1 this partitions all positive indices into disjoint nilpotent chains of length j+h+1. Infinitely many admissible cores c imply all finite lengths with countably infinite multiplicity. Forward and backward cases similarly yield countably infinite shifts. All powers are contractions. Explicit phase vectors and disjoint blocks prove disk lower bounds for polynomial essential norms; von Neumann gives upper bounds. Weyl singular sequences and infinite-dimensional kernel/cokernel prove full Fredholm essential disk. Strong-power statement follows by density on basis and arbitrarily long blocks. The packaged pure-Python checker passes 90,377 finite arithmetic assertions, supplementary only.

value.rationale: The integer pair defines a canonical, motivated product of two common inner-function composition operators; the complete classification collapses infinitely many seemingly different pairs into only four unitary classes. In incomparable pairs, every finite nilpotent block occurs with infinite multiplicity, giving a full-disk essential spectrum and sharp polynomial essential norms despite every nonconstant monomial eventually being killed by a power. These relations are not mere renamings of a generic Halmos–Wallen block but a complete and mathematically explanatory arithmetic realization. Limited to classical unweighted Hardy monomial maps; independent priority assessment remains necessary.
